newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas called a bit lower, cash softens.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas called a bit lower, cash softens.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures were expected to open lower Tuesday due to profit taking and talk of softer cash prices, industry sources said.
July over-the-counter trade ranged from $2.11 to $2.12 after settling to the downside Monday at $2.14 per million British thermal units.
"It's bigger marketers taking profits on short positions," one trader said, noting early Henry Hub cash prices were talked lower at $2.14-2.15 per mmBtu.
On ACCESS, July extended its losses by last trading 1.5 cents lower at $2.125.
Technical traders said support in July was at $2.08. Resistance was still seen at $2.25, and then at $2.37 and the contract high of $2.44.

In Monday's cash, swing gas at the Louisiana Gulf firmed about two cents to the high-teens. Midcon pipes were little changed around $2.02-2.04. New York city gate gas gained about five cents on the heat to the mid-$2.40s.

Above-normal temperatures are forecast to continue across the Northeast and upper Midwest through week's end before turning cooler this weekend and into early next week. In the Southwest, including southern California, temperatures are hovering slightly below normal, Weather Services Corp reported.
Meanwhile, injection estimates for Wednesday's American Gas Association storage report have ranged from 90 to 110 bcf.
